title: streaming: lifecycle controls for client cancel, disconnect, reconnect/resume, and server timeouts
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: production streaming endpoints currently suffer two classes of issues: (1) clients issuing a cancel or becoming disconnected leave server-side resources (KV cache entries, in-flight context) allocated until a fixed server timeout; (2) reconnects/resumes across HTTP streaming and websocket transports are not consistently handled, which breaks OpenAI-compat clients that expect resume semantics. This PR implements a cohesive set of lifecycle controls: explicit client-cancel semantics, robust disconnect detection with graceful cleanup, a reconnect/resume protocol with opaque resume tokens, and configurable server-side timeouts and backoff policies.

What changed (high level):
- Add lifecycle state machine in the serving runtime to track STREAMING_{ACTIVE,CANCELLED,DISCONNECTED,RESUMABLE,EXPIRED}.
- Introduce a short-lived opaque resume token returned to clients on disconnect to allow resumptions within a configurable window. Token format is opaque, HMAC-signed, and versioned for future compatibility.
- Implement explicit client cancel handling on all transports (SSE, HTTP chunked, and WebSocket). Clients can send a final cancel event (or close connection) and server will terminate generation early, emitting a CANCELLED terminal event for telemetry.
- Implement background reclaim for disconnected sessions with a two-phase timeout: soft timeout (default 30s) where we attempt to mark session resumable and persist minimal KV state; hard timeout (default 300s) where we release GPU-backed resources and mark session EXPIRED. Both timeouts are configurable per-route.
- Reconnect/resume protocol: clients present resume token + last-event-id; server validates token and, if valid and within window, resumes from cached KV/decoder state. If resume fails, server falls back to a model-variant or restarts generation depending on policy.
- OpenAI-compat layer updates so streaming resume behavior maps to expected OpenAI semantics (resume via Last-Event-ID and continuation tokens). A compatibility shim ensures older clients get best-effort behavior.
- Expose admin knobs in runtime config and Redwood Console (rollout as a feature flag initially).
- Add extensive unit/integration tests for transport edge cases and flakiness simulations.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- We keep resume tokens short-lived to limit resource locking surface; long resumes would otherwise require keeping large KV caches pinned.
- We deliberately make resume best-effort: resume may be impossible if internal quantized KV state is evicted; in that case we return a structured error advising client on recommended retry semantics.
- For security, resume tokens are HMAC signed against the deployment key and include route/model/version so tokens can't be replayed across customers.
- To avoid latency spikes, reclaim logic is run on a per-GPU background worker with batching of session cleanup.

Rollout plan:
- Start with feature flag off for all production routes. Enable for Canary and Dedicated perf clusters. Monitor cost and error rates.
- Phase 2: enable OpenAI-compat resume behavior for hosted API routes behind an opt-in flag and provide SDK helpers for resume handling.

Backward compatibility:
- Existing clients that simply disconnect will continue to be served; behavior is improved (faster reclaim) but not breaking.
- OpenAI-compat clients that expect resume must be updated to support resume tokens for reliable resumption, but the shim provides best-effort backward compatibility for Last-Event-ID only resumes.

review_comments:
Ravi Kumar: Can we avoid issuing resume tokens for very small sessions (< 3 tokens) to reduce token churn?
Asha: Agreed, added a size-threshold and documented this in lifecycle.rs (config: min_resume_tokens).

Elena Brooks: How do we surface expired sessions to the customer?
Asha: We emit structured events to the console and new metrics (streaming.reclaims.expired) and return a 410-like structured OpenAI-compat error when resume token is invalid/expired.

Samir Desai: CI flakes observed in the websocket tests on the first run. Is this non-determinism from timing?
Asha: Fixed by introducing a deterministic test clock and retry harness in tests/integration/streaming_lifecycle.rs.

Ravi Kumar: Please add a changelog entry and note about opt-in.
Asha: Added release notes and console flag entry.
release_notes: Streaming lifecycle controls: initial implementation of client-cancel, disconnect handling with resumable sessions, configurable soft/hard reclaim timeouts, and OpenAI-compat resume shim. Feature is behind a console feature flag and rolled out to Canary first.
